training_history.opening: Mr. Kumar today. Fifty-two, stomach pain, and a terrible patient. Go on. Ask.

questions.ask: When did the pain start, and has it moved?
questions.answer: Last night, around my belly button. This morning it moved down here, low on the right.
questions.fact: Pain moved from belly button to low right
questions.why: Pain that starts at the belly button and moves low on the right is the classic story of appendicitis.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Penicillin. I came up in a rash once. Big one.
questions.why: He's allergic to penicillin. The usual antibiotic before surgery would have given him a reaction on the table.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: A blood thinner. For my heart. And something for acidity, when I remember.
questions.why: He takes a blood thinner. Operate without knowing and he bleeds, a lot.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Breakfast at eight. Two idlis and tea. Is that bad?
questions.why: He ate at eight. A full stomach under anaesthetic can come back up into the lungs, so surgery has to wait.

questions.ask: Show me exactly where it hurts.
questions.answer: Here. Sharp when I walk, worse when I cough. Don't press it. Don't.
questions.fact: Sharp low right, worse on coughing

questions.ask: Have you had any operations before?
questions.answer: My tonsils. I was eight. I still remember the ice cream.

questions.ask: Do you smoke or drink?
questions.answer: I gave up smoking. Mostly. Weekends don't count.

questions.ask: Do you follow the cricket?
questions.answer: Who doesn't? That's one question gone, Doctor. Patients get tired. So do I.

questions.ask: Is it stressful at work?
questions.answer: I'm a bank manager. Everything is stressful. It's not why my belly hurts.

lakshmi_history.opening: Ask, Doctor. But quickly, before the next one comes. It comes every hour now.

questions.ask: Where is the pain, and when does it come?
questions.answer: Here, under my right ribs. After food, like a fist squeezing. It goes through to my back, up to my shoulder.
questions.fact: Pain under right ribs after meals, into the shoulder
questions.why: Pain under the right ribs after food, going through to the shoulder blade, is the gallbladder's story.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Metformin. For sugar. Please... my son doesn't know. Don't tell Arjun.
questions.fact: Diabetic, on metformin (her son doesn't know)
questions.why: She's diabetic. Her sugar has to be watched around surgery, and metformin is stopped before an anaesthetic.

questions.ask: Any fever or shivering?
questions.answer: Last night I was shaking under two blankets. In this heat!
questions.why: Fever with gallbladder pain means infection. That turns 'come back in six weeks' into 'treat her now'.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Black tea at six. Only tea. I know what fried food does to me now.
questions.why: Black tea at six. Clear drinks are allowed until two hours before an anaesthetic; food waits six.

questions.ask: Has your urine or your skin changed colour?
questions.answer: My urine is dark. Like cola. My skin, I don't know. I don't look in mirrors at my age.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. Only to my son's lectures.

questions.ask: Your son lives in Dubai?
questions.answer: Eleven years. He sends money and opinions. That was a question gone, Doctor.

questions.ask: Do you watch the nine o'clock serial?
questions.answer: Every night. It's not why my stomach hurts.

lakshmi_exam.opening: Gently, Doctor. It's been a long night.

spots.label: Eyes
spots.finding: A faint yellow tinge in the whites of her eyes.
spots.says: My neighbour said I look yellow. I said it's the tube light.
spots.fact: Whites of the eyes slightly yellow
spots.why: Yellow eyes can mean a stone has slipped into the main bile duct. It changes what scan she needs.

spots.label: Temperature
spots.finding: 37.9 degrees. A fever.
spots.why: She has a fever: an infected gallbladder needs antibiotics and surgery soon, not a list in six weeks.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Pulse 98, regular. A little fast.

spots.label: Lower left
spots.finding: Soft. Nothing here.

spots.label: Lower right
spots.finding: Soft, no pain. Not her appendix, then.

spots.label: Upper left
spots.finding: Soft. Nothing to learn here.

spots.label: Upper right
spots.finding: As you press under her ribs she breathes in and stops, mid-breath. Murphy's sign.
spots.says: Aah! Stop, stop. That's the place.
spots.fact: Catches her breath under the right ribs (Murphy's sign)
spots.why: Pressing under the right ribs while she breathed in stopped her short: Murphy's sign, the gallbladder.

diagnoses.why: Right: a stone blocking the gallbladder, now inflamed and infected. Antibiotics, then the gallbladder out.
Not the appendix: her lower right was soft. The pain lives under the ribs.
Worth thinking of in a diabetic, but the pain is pressed out of her right side, not her chest.
Gas doesn't give a fever or Murphy's sign. Sent home, she'd be back tonight, sicker.

kunal_exam.about: 24 · fell off his scooter, right wrist
kunal_exam.opening: Careful! This hand is worth more than your salary. I'm filming this, by the way.

spots.label: Move
spots.finding: He bends and straightens the wrist, wincing at the ends. His grip is strong.
spots.why: He moves it and grips hard. A badly broken wrist rarely lets you do either.

spots.label: Look
spots.finding: Mild swelling on the back of the wrist. No bend, no step. The bones are in line.
spots.why: Look first: no bend and no step. A badly broken wrist looks broken.

spots.label: Snuffbox
spots.finding: You press the hollow at the base of his thumb. He doesn't flinch.
spots.why: The hollow at the base of the thumb hides the scaphoid, a small bone that breaks quietly. His isn't tender.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: A strong pulse at the wrist.

spots.label: Fingers
spots.finding: Warm and pink, and he feels you touch each one.

spots.label: Phone
spots.finding: He's filming you. That's not an examination.
spots.says: Say hi to my eleven thousand followers, Doctor.

diagnoses.why: Right. Swollen, but it moves, it grips, and the snuffbox isn't tender. A splint, ice and painkillers. Then home.
The scaphoid is the one to fear, but his snuffbox wasn't tender. If it were, he'd need a cast and a repeat X-ray.

diagnoses.text: A broken wrist that needs surgery
diagnoses.why: A badly broken wrist is bent and won't grip. His does both. No operation, whoever his uncle is.

rider_exam.opening: A passer-by brought him in. No helmet, no wallet. He's grey, Doctor. Where first?

spots.label: Airway
spots.finding: He groans when you speak to him. The airway is open.
spots.why: Airway always comes early: if he can groan, air is moving.

spots.label: Breathing
spots.finding: Fast, shallow breaths, both sides of the chest moving. Oxygen on.
spots.why: Both sides of his chest move, so no collapsed lung. Oxygen on and move on.

spots.label: Thigh
spots.finding: Bright red blood pumping from a gash in his right thigh. You lean on it with both hands.
spots.fact: Pumping bleed from the right thigh: pressure on
spots.why: His thigh was pumping blood. Hard pressure, early, keeps him alive until theatre.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Fast and thin at the wrist. 128.
spots.why: A fast, weak pulse means he has lost a lot of blood. He needs blood, not just fluids.

spots.label: Head
spots.finding: A graze on his scalp. His pupils react to your torch.

spots.label: Pocket
spots.finding: A cracked phone, buzzing. The screen says: Pooja calling.

diagnoses.text: A torn artery in the thigh
diagnoses.why: Right. A torn artery in the thigh: pressure now, blood on the way, theatre tonight.
The graze bleeds, but his pupils react and he's talking. The thigh is what's killing him.

diagnoses.text: Drunk. Let him sleep it off
diagnoses.why: He's grey because he's bleeding, not because he's drunk. Assume nothing at two in the morning.

joseph_exam.opening: Go ahead, young Doctor. I taught chemistry for thirty-eight years. I can bear a little prodding.

spots.label: Look
spots.finding: His belly is swollen like a drum. An old scar runs down the middle.
spots.says: That? 1987. They took out a bit of my bowel. I kept the rest.
spots.why: An old scar means old surgery, and old surgery leaves bands inside that can kink the bowel: adhesions.

spots.label: Listen
spots.finding: High-pitched tinkling, like water dripping in a pipe.
spots.why: Tinkling sounds mean the bowel is blocked and straining to push past it.

spots.label: Press
spots.finding: Tight, but soft. Sore all over, no one sharp spot.
spots.fact: Tense but soft, no sharp spot

spots.label: Groins
spots.finding: No lump in either groin. Not a trapped hernia.
spots.says: At my age, Doctor, nothing down there surprises me.
spots.why: A trapped hernia in the groin is the other common cause. Always look, however shy the patient.

spots.label: Pulse
spots.finding: Pulse 92, regular.

spots.label: Eyes
spots.finding: His eyes twinkle. That's not a medical finding.
spots.says: Looking for something, Doctor? My reading glasses are on the locker.

diagnoses.text: Bowel blocked by old scar bands (adhesions)
diagnoses.why: Right. Old surgery, a drum-tight belly, tinkling sounds and no hernia: adhesions. A tube and a drip often settle it.
Constipation doesn't make you vomit green or tinkle like a pipe. This is a blockage.
It happens at 81, and a scan will check, but with his scar, adhesions come first. Don't frighten him before you know.

aarav_scan.opening: Aarav's film. Something round in his gullet. Take your time and tell me what it is.

lines.zoom: Look at the edge. Two rings, one inside the other. A halo.
lines.side: From the side it has a step in it. Coins don't have steps.
lines.missed_zoom: You never looked closely: a battery shows a double ring, a halo, at its edge.
lines.missed_side: You never turned to the side view: a battery has a step in it, a coin is one flat line.

answers.text: A coin. It can wait until morning.
answers.why: From the front a battery and a coin look alike. The halo and the step say battery, and waiting would burn through his gullet.

answers.text: A button battery. It comes out now.
answers.why: Right: a button battery. It can burn through the gullet in two hours. Endoscopy, now.
There is something there: the round white shadow in his gullet.

teaching_scan.opening: A teaching film. Ishaan, four, swallowed something at a wedding. Read it properly.

lines.zoom: One clean edge. No second ring.
lines.side: From the side, one thin flat line.
lines.missed_zoom: You never looked closely at the edge: one clean ring is a coin.
lines.missed_side: You never turned to the side view: a coin is one flat line.

answers.why: Right: one clean edge and a flat line from the side. A coin. Most pass on their own.
No halo and no step: it's a coin. Better safe than sorry, but read the film before you call for an endoscopy.
There is something there: a round white shadow in his gullet.

deepa_history.opening: Ask, Doctor. But the lunch rush starts at twelve, and Babu can't make dal.

questions.ask: How did it happen, and when?
questions.answer: A big glass bowl of raita slipped. I caught it. Stupid. An hour ago, not more.
questions.fact: Glass bowl broke in her hand, under an hour ago
questions.why: A fresh wound can be closed today. And broken glass means there may still be glass inside.

questions.ask: Can you move every finger, and feel me touch each one?
questions.answer: They all move. See? The little one feels a bit fuzzy. No. It's fine. Mostly.
questions.fact: Moves every finger, feeling mostly normal
questions.why: Movement and feeling tell you whether a tendon or a nerve is cut, before you go looking inside.

questions.ask: When did you last have a tetanus injection?
questions.answer: Tetanus? In school. Twenty years ago? I was in a green pinafore.
questions.fact: Last tetanus jab about twenty years ago
questions.why: A dirty kitchen wound and twenty years since the last jab: she needs a booster today.

questions.ask: Which hand do you write and chop with?
questions.answer: The right. Of course it's the right.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Only to Babu.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Iron tablets, when I remember. I don't remember.

questions.ask: Is the dal makhani at your dhaba good?
questions.answer: Best on Station Road. Not a medical question, Doctor.

questions.ask: Is someone here with you?
questions.answer: My husband's at the gas agency. He faints at blood. Better he stays there.

bansal_exam.about: 67 · 'kidney stone', back pain into the groin
bansal_exam.opening: Gently, Doctor. The tablets helped, a little. Then they stopped helping.

spots.label: Face
spots.finding: Grey and sweaty. Cold to touch. He looks sicker than a man with a stone should.
spots.says: Is it hot in here? I'm cold. I'm hot. Both.

spots.label: Pressure, pulse
spots.finding: 92 over 58, and a pulse of 116, fast and thready. His notes say he's had high blood pressure for twenty years.
spots.fact: Blood pressure 92/58 in a man who runs high, pulse 116
spots.why: Low pressure and a racing pulse in a man who usually runs high: he's losing blood somewhere you can't see. That's shock.

spots.label: Above the navel
spots.finding: A mass above his navel that pushes your two hands apart with every heartbeat. It pulses, and it swells.
spots.says: Ohh. That's the place. That's where the knife is.
spots.fact: A pulsating, expanding mass above the navel
spots.why: A mass that pushes your hands apart with each beat is a swollen aorta. With low pressure, it's leaking.

spots.label: Groin pulses
spots.finding: The pulses in both groins are weak.
spots.why: Weak pulses in both groins: the blood isn't getting past the aorta. The trouble is upstream, in his belly.

spots.label: Kidney
spots.finding: Over his right kidney from the side: sore, but no worse than anywhere else. A stone usually makes this spot sing.

diagnoses.why: Right: a pulsating mass, low pressure, fast pulse, a smoker over sixty. His aorta is leaking. Vascular surgeons, blood, now.
A first 'kidney stone' in a man over sixty is an aneurysm until you've felt his belly. His pressure was falling.
Back strain doesn't drop the blood pressure or put a pulse in the belly.
His lower right was soft. The pain was in his back and the middle of his belly.

farida_history.opening: Ask away, Doctor. I make my students show their working. You can show yours.

questions.ask: Tell me about the pain attacks.
questions.answer: A year of them. After samosas, mostly. Under my right ribs, then through to my back. The scan showed stones.
questions.fact: A year of gallstone attacks after fatty food
questions.why: A year of attacks with stones on the scan is why she needs the gallbladder out.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines? Even ones you buy yourself?
questions.answer: Only aspirin, for headaches. I took one this morning, in fact. Forty exam papers will do that.
questions.why: Aspirin thins the blood for days. The team needs to know, so they're ready if the liver bed oozes.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. I've checked. I'm a chemist.
questions.why: Now the time-out can confirm 'none known' honestly, because somebody actually asked her.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Dinner at eight last night. Two sips of water at six.
questions.why: Properly fasted: no food for six hours, clear water up to two hours before.

questions.ask: Have you ever turned yellow, or had dark urine?
questions.answer: Never. My skin is this colour by birth, thank you.

questions.ask: Any operations before?
questions.answer: Two caesareans. My children are fourteen and eleven, and louder than Class Ten.

questions.ask: What do you teach?
questions.answer: Chemistry. Twenty years, three lost eyebrows. Not mine.

questions.ask: Have you read about keyhole surgery?
questions.answer: Far too much. Next question, please.

raju_history.about: 38 · stuck lump in the left groin
raju_history.opening: Ask fast, Doctor. Please. It's burning.

questions.ask: Tell me about the lump.
questions.answer: Two years it's been there. It always went back when I lay down. Last night, lifting cement, it came out and stayed.
questions.fact: Hernia for two years, stuck since last night
questions.why: A hernia that suddenly won't go back, with pain, is trapped. The bowel inside can lose its blood supply.

questions.ask: When did you last eat?
questions.answer: A paratha at five. Then I went to the site. Then this.
questions.why: He ate a few hours ago: a full stomach can come up into his lungs under anaesthetic. Dr. Khan must know.

questions.ask: Have you been sick? Opened your bowels?
questions.answer: Sick three times. Green. Nothing out the other end since yesterday.
questions.why: Vomiting and nothing passing means the bowel is blocked where it's trapped.

questions.ask: Are you allergic to anything?
questions.answer: No. Only to my contractor.
questions.why: Asked, so the time-out's 'none known' is the truth and not a guess.

questions.ask: Do you take any medicines?
questions.answer: Nothing. I'm strong like a buffalo. Was.

questions.ask: What work do you do?
questions.answer: Bricks. Cement bags. Fifty kilos each, all day.

questions.ask: Did you watch the match last night?
questions.answer: India lost. That's when the lump came out, I think. Coincidence?

questions.ask: Shall we call someone for you?
questions.answer: My wife. But don't say 'hospital'. Say 'Raju is fine'.
